o1.biggest_strength: Every choice is tied back to the numbers: taste-test/swap openers, label after the sip, price handled on camera in scripts 1 and 2, and three genuinely different angles built from real customer lines.
o1.biggest_mistake: Dense and slightly overloaded; the timing table plus long briefs plus a test plan pushes against the 1,300-word limit and grade-6 reading level, and a couple of spoken lines run long for their time slots.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Trim to the word limit and tighten each spoken block so every line actually fits its seconds, keeping the same data-backed logic.

o2.biggest_strength: Clean, readable, easy to shoot: clear rules, tight hook sets, and the #ad/disclosure handled cleanly; scripts read fast and match the 30-45s format.
o2.biggest_mistake: Thinner insight and less price handling: only one script really answers the $3-a-can objection, the family script's claims moment is fumbled (it drops real fruit juice into the label read but skips the price context), and the test plan is generic with no budget or thresholds.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Put price objection handling into more than one script and give the hook test real numbers, thresholds and a kill rule drawn from the 60-day data.

reason: Output 1 reads like someone who read my data and built the scripts around it, including the price objection and a test plan with real thresholds; Output 2 is crisper to read but feels more like good scripts than a plan I'd bet money on.
